title: Speiz — Commercial Real Estate Platform
headline: Making warehouse search faster and more transparent in a fragmented B2B market

overview.headline: Helping tenants move from space requirements to relevant options

intro: Speiz is a B2B commercial real estate platform that helps businesses discover, evaluate, and connect with warehouse spaces across Norway.
Warehouse search relied on listings, PDFs, brokers, and direct landlord communication, making it slow to identify and qualify relevant spaces.

sections.label: ROLE & SCOPE
sections.headline: Working across design, product, and delivery
paragraphs: I owned major parts of the tenant experience end to end, from research and product flows to detailed UI, requirements, delivery, and iteration. As the product evolved, I also took on product management responsibilities, helping shape priorities and working across design, development, and business.

sections.label: PROBLEM
sections.headline: Building a viable shortlist required days of manual verification
paragraphs: Finding a warehouse often meant piecing together information from multiple listing platforms, PDFs, brokers, and direct conversations with landlords. Before tenants could evaluate an option, they first had to verify whether basic property information was current and complete, including availability, specifications, imagery, and pricing.

items.title: Scattered market data
items.text: Property information was spread across multiple listing platforms and sources.

items.title: Unclear availability
items.text: Vacancy was not always visible or reliably up to date.

items.title: Missing specifications
items.text: Important operational details were often incomplete or absent.

items.title: Outdated visuals
items.text: Images did not always reflect the current condition of the space.

items.title: PDF-heavy evaluation
items.text: Tenants had to compare multiple documents to understand basic details.

items.title: Broker-led communication
items.text: Clarifying basic information often required long email chains and manual follow-up.

sections.headline: Understanding the market before defining the product
paragraphs: We looked at the warehouse-search journey from several angles: how tenants evaluated spaces, how existing platforms structured the market, and how commercial property data could be accessed at scale.

sections.label: DESIGN PROCESS
sections.headline: Structuring the journey from requirement to connection
paragraphs: Research helped define what the product needed to solve. The next challenge was turning those findings into a coherent journey that could support discovery, evaluation, and decision-making without overwhelming the user.

blocks.title: Information architecture
blocks.description: Organising market data, property information, requests, and user actions into a structure that could scale as the product evolved.

blocks.title: Core flows
blocks.description: Mapping how tenants moved between search, recommendations, property evaluation, and decision-making.

blocks.title: Product system
blocks.description: Translating the core flows into reusable interface patterns for search, filtering, property evaluation, and user actions.

sections.label: FINAL SOLUTION

children.label: FINAL SOLUTION
children.headline: Three ways to reach a relevant shortlist
paragraphs: Once users could explore the product before registering, the next challenge was supporting different ways of finding relevant spaces. Speiz offered three discovery paths built on the same market data: direct search, human curation, and AI-assisted matching.

items.title: Classic Search
items.text: For tenants with clear criteria who want direct control over search and filtering.

items.title: Speiz Picks
items.text: A shortlist manually curated by the Speiz team for a specific tenant request.

items.title: AI Matches
items.text: Natural-language requirements turned into ranked, explained recommendations.

blocks.headline: Direct market access for tenants who know what they need
paragraphs: For tenants with clear requirements, Classic Search provided direct access through structured filters, property results, and a map. Users could narrow options by criteria such as location, size, and move-in date, then explore relevant spaces independently.

items.title: Structured filters
items.description: Refine the market using known requirements.

items.title: Map + results
items.description: Understand available supply and location together.

items.title: Comparable listings
items.description: See essential property information before opening a space.

children.label: SPEIZ PICKS
children.headline: Adding human expertise when search alone wasn't enough
paragraphs: Not every tenant wanted to search the entire market independently. Speiz Picks introduced a guided experience where the Speiz team reviewed a tenant’s requirements, searched the market, and curated a shortlist specifically for that request.

items.title: Guided process
items.description: Understand the tenant’s needs through a personal call and market review.

items.title: Curated shortlist
items.description: Review spaces selected specifically for the original request.

items.title: Feedback loop
items.description: Accept, reject, and comment on recommendations directly in the product.

children.label: AI MATCHES
children.headline: Turning a natural-language brief into explainable recommendations
paragraphs: Instead of translating every requirement into filters, tenants could describe what they needed in natural language. AI Matches turned that brief into a ranked shortlist and explained how each space matched the request.

items.title: Natural-language brief
items.description: Describe operational requirements in everyday language instead of building a complex filter set.

items.title: Ranked shortlist
items.description: Surface the most relevant spaces first using the tenant’s original requirements.

base.alt: Speiz AI Matches — Ranked shortlist&Explanable matching

items.title: Explainable matching
items.description: Show why each space fits, where information is missing, and which sources support the recommendation.

base.alt: Speiz AI Matches — Ranked shortlist&Explanable matching

children.label: SPACE DETAILS
children.headline: Everything needed to evaluate a space in one place
paragraphs: We therefore focused on bringing the information needed for early evaluation into a structured property experience rather than forcing users to move between listings, PDFs, and broker communication.

image.alt: Full Speiz Space Details page showing property imagery, specifications, facilities, location, viewing request and landlord contact.

features.title: Full specifications
features.text: Review size, facilities, loading access, ceiling height, property type, and other operational details.

features.title: Current property visuals
features.text: See recent photos and understand the space before arranging a visit.

features.title: Availability & pricing
features.text: Check availability, move-in timing, and expected pricing without additional back-and-forth.

features.title: Direct next steps
features.text: Book a viewing or contact the landlord directly when a space looks relevant.

children.label: MESSAGES
children.headline: Keeping the conversation inside the product
paragraphs: Once a tenant decided to move forward with a space, the journey continued inside Speiz. Messages kept the conversation with the landlord in the same product context instead of pushing users back into disconnected email threads.

image.alt: Speiz Messages interface with conversation list, landlord chat, and details of the space being discussed.

features.title: Space context
features.text: Keep the conversation connected to the specific space being discussed.

features.title: Direct communication
features.text: Message the landlord without leaving the product.

features.title: Conversation history
features.text: Keep previous questions and responses in one place instead of scattered email threads.

features.title: Next steps
features.text: Continue from interest to viewing, clarification, and follow-up without losing context.

sections.headline: Opening the product before asking users to commit
paragraphs: We moved registration from the start of the journey to the moment of intent. Instead of asking users to sign up before seeing value, tenants could explore and evaluate the market first, registering only when they wanted to connect.

image.alt: Speiz before redesign: Onboarding · Space requirements.

sections.label: IMPACT
sections.headline: From registration-first to value-first product experience
paragraphs: Speiz evolved from a landing-page-led, registration-first journey into an open product experience where tenants could explore the market, evaluate spaces, and choose how to reach a shortlist before being asked to register at the moment of intent.

items.title: Open access before registration
items.text: Users could explore relevant spaces and see product value before being asked to create an account.

items.title: Broader market coverage in one place
items.text: Connecting Speiz to a nationwide commercial real estate database gave tenants a broader view of the Norwegian market within a single product.

items.title: Decision-ready property information
items.text: Availability, specifications, pricing, and current visuals were structured around what tenants needed to evaluate a space.

items.title: Faster path from search to viewing
items.text: Search, availability checks, and viewing coordination moved into one flow, reducing weeks of back-and-forth across different channels.

items.title: Multiple paths to a shortlist
items.text: Users could search independently, use AI-assisted matching, or rely on a shortlist curated by the Speiz team when they needed more guidance.

items.title: Connected follow-up
items.text: Viewing requests and landlord conversations could continue inside Speiz instead of moving back into disconnected email threads.

sections.label: BEYOND THE TENANT EXPERIENCE
sections.headline: Designing for the wider product ecosystem

paragraphs: This case study focuses on the tenant journey, but Speiz supported a broader product ecosystem. I also designed landlord-facing and internal admin experiences that supported day-to-day operations across the platform.
Designing across these different sides of the product required considering how actions and information in one interface affected the others.
